content:
maya: Heads up — CI for infra/gpu-clusters is failing on the GH Actions 'apply' job. Seen a bunch of helm syncs waiting and terraform stuck on rollout.

maya: Root log: 
```
Error: no nodes match node selector: accelerator == nvidia && gpu_pool == dedicated
Waiting for 300s for pods to be scheduled...
helm: timed out waiting for condition
terraform: resource stuck waiting for kubernetes_deployment rollout
```

devon: I saw the same. Looks like autoscaler added nodes but the node labels aren't matching the selector used in our taint/toleration & nodeSelector. Suspect cloud-init/packer image change. :thinking_face:

sam: Quick check — can you paste output of `kubectl get nodes --show-labels` from the job logs? CI runner masks kubeconfig but gha-bot sometimes posts node list. gha-bot: posting last-known node list from last successful canary: 
```
node-23   Ready   gpu;accelerator=nvidia;gpu_pool=spot
node-24   Ready   gpu;accelerator=NVIDIA;gpu_pool=dedicated
node-25   NotReady   gpu;accelerator=nvidia;gpu_pool=dedicated
```

devon: Ah, there's the problem — label case mismatch on `accelerator` value ("NVIDIA" vs "nvidia") and a missing `gpu_pool` label on node-23. Our helm chart nodeSelector is `accelerator: "nvidia"` and `gpu_pool: "dedicated"`. Kubernetes label values are case-sensitive.

ops-anne: How did this get past canary? Did node bootstrap change? I remember an image update last night that touches `metadata.sh` which writes labels.

maya: yeah, packer -> image-build 2026-03-15 bumped cloud-init script. New nodes now set `accelerator` to upper case in some regions due to provider metadata.

sam: Short-term fix: update helm chart to be more permissive (use nodeAffinity with matchExpressions so we can OR? or only check `gpu_pool`). But changing chart in CI might hide underlying drift.

devon: I propose: 1) patch node labels in cluster (imperative) for the affected nodes to match existing selector, 2) revert image change in image-build pipeline and add test in infra-ci to verify node labels, 3) add a graceful fallback to our helm values to prefer `gpu_pool` only.

ops-anne: I'll patch nodes now: `kubectl label node node-24 accelerator=nvidia --overwrite` and `kubectl label node node-23 gpu_pool=dedicated --overwrite` — doing it from jumpbox. Will post results.

ops-anne: patched. rerunning GH Actions apply...

gha-bot: Workflow run 2345 re-triggered by ops-anne. Job: infra-apply (runner: gha-selfhosted-gpu).

maya: apply is progressing — helm sync now moving past `Waiting for pods` step. No more `no nodes match` in logs.

sam: For long-term: add a CI check in `infra-ci/validate-node-labels` that spins up a tiny nodepool in a sandbox and validates labels from the image. Also add an integration test step in image-build to assert `accelerator` lowercase.

devon: Filed a PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 — adds node-label unit check in image-build and a GH Action in infra repo to lint cluster labels (non-blocking for now).

maya: Also adding a post-deploy smoke check to the apply job: after helm apply wait, run `kubectl get pods -l app=gpu-worker -o wide` and assert >0 pods Running. If not, fail faster.

ops-anne: Sounds good. I'll roll back the image build change and coordinate with infra-sre to test in staging.

devon: Leaving a note in the release notes / runbook: "If CI fails with node selector errors, check node labels for case-sensitivity and gpu_pool presence; patch or rollback image; run label-validator."

maya: Thanks all :thumbsup: We'll monitor next runs. If flaky recurs, escalate to infra-ml for autoscaler metadata handling.
